NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learner with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development

in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that Learner shall proceed to after the Pre- Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre-career

experience in which Learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated interest and/or

potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age bracket and lays

the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this level are

expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, Learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms(PWPER,

2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core Mathematics and

Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science Technology

Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). Learner will select three

learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, Learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT FOR HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP

The History and Citizenship curriculum for Senior School is structured around four broad strands, each designed to build upon

cumulative knowledge and understanding of various themes. This curriculum emphasizes the importance of understanding the

past to better comprehend the present and envision the future. History offers valuable insights into human behaviour, societal

norms, and the consequences of past actions. By exploring historical events, students develop critical thinking skills, learn to

analyse complex information, and cultivate a broader perspective on the world around them.

Citizenship education in Senior School plays a pivotal role in shaping responsible and active members of society. It provides

students with a clear understanding of their rights and responsibilities, fosters a sense of civic duty, and nurtures skills essential

for effective participation in a democratic society. Additionally, History offers insights into historical struggles for justice and

equality, empowering students to become advocates for positive change in their communities and beyond.

The essence of studying History and Citizenship in Senior School is to shape the future through informed decision-making and

active citizenship. By embracing the interconnectedness of history and citizenship, students embark on a transformative

educational journey that equips them with the tools to navigate an ever-changing world with curiosity, empathy, and resilience.

Assessment is an integral part of the History and Citizenship learning process. Assessment practices in these subjects will focus

on assessing learning and providing timely, comprehensive feedback. This feedback motivates students to achieve their goals in

History and Citizenship. The assessments are designed to evaluate students' application of values and the development of social

and emotional competencies, as well as skills related to both History and Citizenship. As such, the study of History and Citizenship

is central as a hub for cross-curricular connections.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior Secondary School, Learner should be able to:

1. Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of key themes in Kenyan history and citizenship.

2. Explore Kenya's position in regional and global contexts, recognizing its contributions to peace-building, governance, and

international cooperation.

3. Demonstrate a deep understanding of the diverse African civilizations, their cultural contributions, and the historical

processes of colonization, independence, and post-colonial transformation.

4. Critically analyse the social, political, and economic changes in African societies, recognizing the lasting impact of

colonialism and the ongoing efforts towards African unity, development, and self-determination.

5. Examine the role of African citizens in promoting good governance, peace-building, and sustainable development, both at

national and regional levels.

6. Analyse significant global events, such as revolutions, wars, and the rise of empires, and assess their impact on shaping

modern societies, international relations, and world systems.

7. Examine key global movements and institutions that promote equality, democracy, and peace, and understand the roles of

individuals and nations in addressing contemporary global challenges such as poverty, climate change, and conflict

resolution.

8. Conduct research and analyse the major political, social, and technological transformations of the contemporary world.

9. Explore the impact of globalization, the rise of digital technologies, and the evolution of global economies, while

understanding the role of contemporary social movements in advocating for human rights, equality, and environmental

sustainability.

10. Exhibit an understanding of the responsibilities of citizenship in the modern world.

11. Recognise the role of individuals in democratic processes, social justice advocacy, and global governance, and actively

engage in discussions on how to promote civic participation, social equity, and peace in their communities and the wider

world.

iii

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races, and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They

must be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of

nationhood by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism, and to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships, which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid

modernisation. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required

to support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya

recognises the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be

part of this development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will

prepare our young people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

iv

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children

to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

4. Promote sound moral and religious values

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound

moral values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities

and corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the

contemporary society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must

follow rapid development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

v

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to

after the Pre-Primary School, Primary School, and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre- tertiary/university/ pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks, and subjects where

they shall have demonstrated interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for

learners in the 16-18 years age bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world

of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to

participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational

Reforms (PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential

Mathematics/Core Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for

learners pursuing the Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners

pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest

and personality with guidance by the Senior School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical, and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

vi

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education, and training,

5. uphold national, moral, and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve, and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

The Senior School English curriculum is designed to build upon the foundational linguistic and communicative competencies

developed at the Junior School level. These early skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing provide a solid base for learners

to engage with English as a tool for communication, a medium of instruction, and a subject of academic study.

At the Senior School level, the English language educators are expected to use transformative pedagogical approaches grounded

in contemporary linguistic and language learning theories. Teachers could employ methodologies such as Experiential Learning,

Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Project-Based Learning, Collaborative Learning, Reflective Learning, and Communicative

Language Teaching coupled with the innovative use of ICTs to pique the learner’s interest and enhance proficiency. Classroom

strategies may include journaling, peer and self-assessment, lesson recordings for reflection, case studies, storytelling, simulations,

role play, hot seating, reader’s theater and structured debates. These approaches are intended to create dynamic, learner-centred

environments that promote both linguistic competency and metacognitive awareness. Beyond the classroom, educators are

encouraged to facilitate learners’ participation in non-formal and informal language-rich activities such as drama and music

festivals, public speaking events, debates, and involvement in clubs and societies. These experiences provide authentic contexts

for language use and help learners connect English to real-world applications.

Given the status of English as the global lingua franca in domains such as diplomacy, commerce, technology, and international

relations, proficiency in the language opens diverse academic and career pathways, by the end of Senior School. These advanced

English language skills are necessary for further education and professional pursuits in fields such as law, journalism, marketing,

advertising, public relations, editing, research, linguistics, teaching, lexicography, translation, and the performing arts.

x

GENERAL SUBJECT LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR ENGLISH

By the end of the course, the learner should be able to:

1. use verbal and nonverbal cues appropriately for speaking fluency,

2. listen to varied oral texts for comprehension,

3. speak on a wide range of subjects fluently and confidently,

4. apply knowledge of grammar in oral and written texts,

5. develop a wide range of vocabulary for use in formal and informal discourse,

6. read a range of texts for information and pleasure including texts from contrasting times and cultures,

7. write creative, functional, and argumentative texts for varied purposes and audiences,

8. utilise ICTs innovatively to convey oral and written information.

xi

THEMES

In the Grade 12 English Curriculum, the following themes will facilitate the learning of English in context:

1.0 Etiquette: Courtesy in road and air travel

2.0 Environment: Green technology and eco-friendly solutions

3.0 AI and creativity: Innovative and ethical use of AI

4.0 The future of travel: Space exploration and tourism

5.0 Skills for the future: Soft and hard skills

6.0 Culture and power: Whose voices matter?

7.0 Sports and games: Career opportunities

8.0 Health and safety: Food safety and hygiene

9.0 The Digital Economy: Digital financial services

Note:

Learning in the four language domains—listening, speaking, reading, and writing—together with the foundational aspects of

grammar and vocabulary, does not occur in isolation. Instead, these skills are taught and learnt within the context of a chosen

theme.

This means that the learner listens to language related to the theme and then speaks, reads, and writes about ideas and situations

connected to that same theme. Grammar and vocabulary are also introduced and practised using relevant examples drawn from

the theme.

In simple terms, strands represent the language skills, while themes provide the contexts in which the learner develops and applies

these skills. This approach enables the learner to understand and use language meaningfully, rather than memorising it without

context.

MALENGO YA KITAIFA YA ELIMU NCHINI KENYA

Elimu nchini Kenya inatakiwa:

1. Kukuza na kustawisha utaifa, uzalendo na kuendeleza umoja wa kitaifa

Nchini Kenya kuna jamii zenye mila, dini na tamaduni mbalimbali lakini tofauti hizi hazifai kuzitenganisha. Lazima waweze kuishi

na kutangamana kama Wakenya. Elimu ina jukumu kuu la kuwezesha vijana kujenga hisia za uzalendo na utaifa kwa kuondoa

mivutano na kukuza mielekeo chanya ya kuheshimiana itakayowezesha jamii kuishi pamoja kwa utangamano na kujenga uzalendo

ili kuchangia uhai wa taifa.

2. Kukidhi mahitaji ya kijamii, kiuchumi, kiteknolojia na viwanda yanayochangia maendeleo ya kitaifa

Elimu inafaa kuwaandaa vijana wa nchi kutekeleza wajibu wenye umuhimu katika maisha nchini.

a) Mahitaji ya kijamii

Elimu nchini Kenya lazima iwatayarishe vijana kwa mabadiliko ya mielekeo na mahusiano ambayo yanahitajika kwa maendeleo

ya haraka ya uchumi wa kisasa. Kuna uwezekano wa kuwa na mapinduzi kimyakimya ya kijamii kutokana na maendeleo ya

haraka ya usasa. Elimu inapaswa kuwasaidia vijana kujirekekebisha kutokana na mabadiliko haya.

b) Mahitaji ya kiuchumi

Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kukuza raia walio na stadi, maarifa, ujuzi na sifa za kibinafsi zinazohitajika kuhimili maendeleo ya

kiuchumi. Kenya inajenga uchumi huru na wa kisasa ambao unahitaji wafanyakazi wa kutosha, walio na maarifa yanayohitajika

na wa humu nchini.

c) Mahitaji ya kiteknolojia na ya kiviwanda

Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kuwapa vijana stadi na mielekeo inayohitajika kwa maendeleo ya kiviwanda. Kenya

inatambua mabadiliko ya haraka ya kiviwanda na kiteknolojia yanayofanyika, hasa katika ulimwengu ulioendelea. Tunaweza

kuwa sehemu ya maendeleo haya ikiwa mfumo wetu wa elimu utalenga kimakusudi maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayotayarisha

vijana kwa mabadiliko ya yanayoendelea ulimwenguni.

3. Kutoa nafasi ya kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza

Elimu inapaswa kumwezesha mtu kutambua, kukuza na kuimarisha kipawa chake ili aweze kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza. Inafaa

kuwawezesha watoto kukuza uwezo wao. Kipengele muhimu cha maendeleo ya kibinafsi ni ujenzi wa tabia ifaayo.

iii

4. Kuwawezesha wananchi kuimarisha maadili na amali za kijamii na kidini

Elimu inakusudiwa kukuza maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayoimarisha upataji wa maadili na kuwasaidia watoto kukua wakiwa

wenye nidhamu, wanaojitegemea na raia wakamilifu.

5. Kuimarisha usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji

Usawa wa kijamii kwa mfano usawa wa kijinsia huimarika watu wa jamii na jinsia zote wanapopata elimu sawa. Elimu inafaa ikuze

usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji wa kijamii kutokana na mfumo wa elimu unaowezesha fursa sawa ya elimu kwa wote. Inafaa

kuwapa watoto wote fursa mbalimbali na zilizo na changamoto kwa mazoezi ya pamoja na ushirika katika huduma za kijamii bila

kujali jinsia, uwezo au mazingira ya kijiografia.

6. Kukuza uthamini wa tamaduni mbalimbali nchini Kenya

Elimu inafaa kutoa nafasi kwa wanaosoma kuelewa, kuthamini, kukuza na kudumisha tamaduni faafu na kudondoa zile potofu

kulingana na jamii ya wakati uliopo ili kujenga jamii ya kisasa.

7. Kuimarisha utambuzi wa uhusiano wa kimataifa na kukuza mwelekeo chanya kwa mataifa mengine

Kenya kama nchi mojawapo ya jamii ya kimataifa inakusudia elimu iwaelekeze Wakenya kutambua na kuthamini mahusiano ya

kimataifa kwa kuzingatia mikataba, uwajibikaji, haki na manufaa yanayoambatana na ushirika huo.

8. Kustawisha mwelekeo chanya kuhusu afya bora na uhifadhi wa mazingira

Elimu inakusudiwa kujenga mielekeo ifaayo miongoni mwa vijana kuhusu udumishaji wa afya bora na mazingira kwa kujiepusha

na mienendo inayoweza kudhuru afya ya mwili na akili. Elimu inafaa pia kuimarisha mielekeo chanya kuhusu ukuzaji na uhifadhi

wa mazingira. Inafaa kuwaelekeza vijana wa Kenya kukubali haja ya mazingira safi.

DARAJA YA JUU SHULE ZA UPILI KATIKA MTAALA WA KIUMILISI

Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili, ni kiwango cha nne cha Elimu ya Msingi katika Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) ambayo wanafunzi

watajiunga nayo baada ya kumaliza Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi, na Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu la Daraja ya Shule za Upili ni

kuwapa wanafunzi uzoefu wa awali wa chuo kikuu au taaluma, ambapo wanafunzi wanapata fursa ya kuchagua mielekeo na nyanja

wanazovutiwa nazo na walizoonyesha uwezo katika viwango vya awali. Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili inajumuisha miaka mitatu

ya masomo kwa wanafunzi walio kati ya umri wa miaka 16-18 na huweka msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi, mafunzo ya kitaaluma,

na ulimwengu wa kazi. Katika ruwaza ya Mtaala wa Kiumilisi, wanafunzi watakaohitimu katika kiwango hiki wanatarajiwa kuwa

raia waliohusishwa, waliowezeshwa, na waadilifu walio tayari kushiriki katika maendeleo ya kijamii na kiuchumi ya taifa.

Katika kiwango hiki, wanafunzi watajifunza masomo saba (7) kama yalivyopendekezwa na Kamati ya Rais ya Mageuzi ya Elimu

(PWPER,2023). Masomo haya yanajumuisha masomo manne ya lazima ambayo ni: English, Kiswahili, Essential

Mathematics/Core Mathematics na Community Service Learning – CSL. Wanafunzi watachagua kati ya Core Mathematics (kwa

wanafunzi wanaofuatilia mkondo wa STEM) na Essential Mathematics (kwa wanafunzi wanaofuatilia mikondo isiyo ya STEM).

Wanafunzi watachagua masomo mengine matatu kulingana na chaguo la taaluma, vipaji, mapendeleo yao kwa somo fulani, na

haiba zao, wakisaidiwa na mwalimu wao wa Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili.

Kufikia mwisho wa Daraja ya Juu Shule za Upili, mwanafunzi aweze:

2. kutumia maarifa ya kihisabati, kimantiki na uwazaji kina katika utatuzi wa matatizo,

7. kulinda, kuhifadhi na kuboresha mazingira kwa ajili ya uendelevu,

9. kuonyesha uthamini wa tofauti za watu na tamaduni,

10. kuonyesha uwajibikaji katika kushughulikia masuala mtambuko

KAULI KIINI

Somo la Fasihi ya Kiswahili katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili linaendeleza maarifa na ujuzi ambao mwanafunzi amepata

katika Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu ni kumwezesha mwanafunzi kupanua uelewa wake kuhusu fasihi, si tu kama sanaa ya lugha bali

pia kama chombo cha kuelewa na kushirikiana na tamaduni mbalimbali. Mabadiliko haya kutoka Shule ya Junia hadi daraja ya

juu huambatana na upanuzi wa dhana, stadi, na mwelekeo wa kifasihi. Wanafunzi hujifunza kwa kina kuhusu tanzu mbalimbali

za fasihi kama vile ushairi, riwaya, tamthilia, hadithi fupi, kazi za kihalisia na fasihi simulizi. Somo hili hulenga kukuza uwezo

wa mwanafunzi wa kusoma kwa kina, kutathmini na kuhakiki kazi za fasihi kwa kuzingatia muktadha wa kijamii, kiutamaduni na

kihistoria. Aidha, somo hili huwasaidia wanafunzi kutambua nafasi ya fasihi kama sanaa ya lugha na kama chombo cha

kuwasilisha, kuhifadhi, na kuendeleza maadili na tamaduni za jamii mbalimbali.

Mbinu za ujifunzaji katika somo hili zinalenga kumwandaa mwanafunzi kwa hatua inayofuata ya kielimu na kimaisha. Ufundishaji

huhusisha ushirikishwaji wa wanafunzi kupitia mijadala ya kina, uchambuzi wa matini, uandishi wa kazi za kiubunifu na

utekelezaji wa miradi ya kifasihi. Vilevile, wanafunzi watashiriki matukio ya kifasihi kama vile maonyesho ya kazi za kibunilizi,

mashindano ya ushairi na makongamano ya kielimu ili kukuza stadi za uwasilishaji na kuwapa wanafunzi uwezo wa kufikiri kwa

kina, kuwasiliana kwa ufasaha, na kushirikiana na wengine katika mazingira tofauti ya kijamii na kitaaluma. Hali hii huwajengea

misingi imara ya kujiamini na kuwa raia wenye mchango chanya katika jamii yao na ulimwenguni kwa jumla.

Kufikia mwisho wa kozi, mwanafunzi anatarajiwa kuwa amefikia kiwango cha juu cha umahiri katika Fasihi ya Kiswahili. Hali

hii itamfungulia fursa za ajira katika taaluma kama vile uandishi wa habari, tafsiri, uchapishaji, utafiti wa kifasihi, ufundishaji,

sanaa za maonyesho, burudani na utangazaji.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid

modernisation. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya

recognizes the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part

of this development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our

young people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help

children to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the

contemporary society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must

follow rapid development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after

the Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre- tertiary/university/ pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where

they shall have demonstrated interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for

learners generally in the 16-18 years age bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the

world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to

participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational

Reforms (PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential

Mathematics/Core Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for

learners pursuing the Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing

the non-STEM pathways). The learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and

personality with guidance by the Senior School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

The Indigenous Languages curriculum design has been designed to equip learners with the requisite knowledge, skills and

attitudes required to participate in various social activities and interact with each other and the environment in which they live. It

builds on the language skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing handled at the Junior School level. Grammar is also a

key strand in the design as it supports the development of literacy and communication skills. The course will strengthen positive

attitudes and behaviour towards active listening and speaking, as well as extensive and intensive reading in indigenous language

in anticipation of the successful discovery of information. The writing types provided are tailored towards developing skills that

can be applied to real-life situations and the world of work.

The learner will be exposed to multiple ways of accessing information to improve learning. They will be inspired to embrace

effective learning strategies such as carrying out projects and participating in indigenous language-based programmes in and out

of school. Consequently, learning and communicating effectively in their indigenous language will be an added advantage. The

use of the thematic language teaching will ensure that the requisite concepts, skills and attitudes are acquired within meaningful

contexts and that the learner interacts with pertinent issues at community, national and global level.

By the end of the course, the learner will be expected to have attained high proficiency in the use of their indigenous language.

This will open career opportunities in the media and other fields such as translation, publishing, research, law, teaching,

indigenous science and technologies, medicine and public relations. Learners could for instance advance their knowledge of the

indigenous language to become linguists who specialise in the development of orthographies.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Express themselves confidently and appropriately in a variety of social contexts

2. Apply the use of indigenous language in various communication situations

3. Demonstrate ability to apply indigenous knowledge, culture and values in varied situations

4. Comprehend information in different contexts in the indigenous language

5. Read fluently with comprehension in indigenous language

6. Use indigenous language to legibly write ideas and opinions in different formats

7. Enjoy communicating using a variety of cultural language strategies.

MALENGO YA KITAIFA YA ELIMU NCHINI KENYA

Elimu nchini Kenya inatakiwa:

1. Kukuza na kustawisha utaifa, uzalendo na kuendeleza umoja wa kitaifa

Nchini Kenya kuna jamii zenye mila, dini na tamaduni mbalimbali lakini tofauti hizi hazifai kuzitenganisha. Lazima waweze

kuishi na kutangamana kama Wakenya. Elimu ina jukumu kuu la kuwezesha vijana kujenga hisia za uzalendo na utaifa kwa

kutatua mivutano na kukuza mielekeo chanya ya kuheshimiana. Mielekeo hii itawawezesha wanajamii kuishi pamoja kwa

utangamano na kujenga uzalendo ili kuchangia ukuaji wa taifa.

2. Kukidhi mahitaji ya kijamii, kiuchumi, kiteknolojia na viwanda yanayochangia maendeleo ya kitaifa

Elimu inafaa kuwaandaa vijana wa taifa la Kenya kutekeleza wajibu wenye umuhimu katika maisha nchini.

a) Mahitaji ya kijamii

Elimu nchini Kenya lazima iwatayarishe vijana kwa mabadiliko ya mielekeo na mahusiano ambayo yanahitajika kwa

maendeleo ya haraka ya uchumi wa kisasa. Kuna uwezekano wa kuwa na mageuzi taratibu ya kijamii kutokana na

maendeleo ya usasa yanayojitokeza kwa kasi. Elimu inapaswa kuwasaidia vijana kuwa na uwezo wa kukabiliana na

mabadiliko haya.

b) Mahitaji ya kiuchumi

Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kukuza raia walio na stadi, maarifa, ujuzi na uwezo wa kibinafsi unaohitajika kuhimili

maendeleo ya kiuchumi. Kenya inajenga uchumi huru na wa kisasa ambao unahitaji wafanyakazi wa kutosha, walio na

maarifa yanayohitajika humu nchini.

c) Mahitaji ya kiteknolojia na ya kiviwanda

Elimu nchini Kenya inafaa kuwapa vijana stadi na mielekeo inayohitajika kwa maendeleo ya kiviwanda. Kenya

inatambuamabadiliko ya kasi ya kiviwanda na kiteknolojia yanayofanyika, hasa katika ulimwengu ulioendelea. Tunahitaji

kuwasehemu ya maendeleo haya ili mfumo wetu wa elimu ulenge kimakusudi maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayotayarisha

vijana kwa mabadiliko yanayoendelea ulimwenguni.

3. Kutoa nafasi ya kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza

Elimu inapaswa kuwezesha kutambua, kukuza na kuimarisha vipawa vya kila mmoja ili kuweza kujiendeleza na kujitosheleza.

iv

Inafaa kuwawezesha watoto kukuza uwezo wao. Kipengele muhimu cha maendeleo ya kibinafsi ni ujenzi wa tabia ifaayo.

4. Kuwawezesha wananchi kuimarisha maadili na amali za kijamii na kidini

Elimu inakusudiwa kukuza maarifa, stadi na mielekeo itakayoimarisha upataji wa maadili na kuwasaidia watoto kukua wakiwa

wenye nidhamu, wanaojitegemea na raia wakamilifu.

5. Kuimarisha usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji

Usawa wa kijamii kwa mfano, usawa wa kijinsia huimarika watu wa jamii na jinsia zote wanapopata elimu sawa. Elimu inafaa

ikuze usawa wa kijamii na uwajibikaji wa kijamii kutokana na mfumo wa elimu unaowezesha fursa sawa ya elimu kwa wote.

Inafaa kuwapa watoto wote fursa mbalimbali na zenye changamoto zitakazowawezesha kutoa huduma jumuishi za kijamii bila

kujali jinsia, uwezo au mazingira ya kijiografia.

6. Kukuza uthamini wa tamaduni mbalimbali nchini Kenya

Elimu inafaa kuwapa vijana uelewa wa tamaduni za kale na za sasa na nafasi yazo katika jamii ya kisasa. Watoto wanafaa

kuambatanisha maadili ya tamaduni bora na mahitaji yanayobadilika kulingana na maendeleo yanayotokea ili kujenga jamii

thabiti ya kisasa.

7. Kuimarisha utambuzi wa uhusiano wa kimataifa na kukuza mwelekeo chanya kwa mataifa mengine

Kenya ni sehemu ya jamii ya kimataifa. Ni sehemu ya mtandao changamano unaotegemeana wa watu na mataifa. Kwa hivyo,

elimu inapaswa kuwaelekeza vijana kukubali uanachama wa jamii hii ya kimataifa pamoja na majukumu na uwajibikaji, haki

na manufaa ambayo yanatokana na uanachama huu.

8. Kustawisha mwelekeo chanya kuhusu afya bora na uhifadhi wa mazingira

Elimu inakusudiwa kujenga mielekeo ifaayo miongoni mwa vijana kuhusu udumishaji wa afya bora na mazingira kwa

kujiepusha na mienendo inayoweza kudhuru afya ya mwili na akili. Aidha, inafaa kuimarisha mielekeo chanya kuhusu ukuzaji

na uhifadhi wa mazingira na kuwaelekeza vijana kuthamini usafi wa mazingira.

DARAJA YA JUU YA SHULE ZA UPILI KATIKA MTAALA WA KIUMILISI

Daraja ya juu ya shule za upili, ni kiwango cha nne cha Elimu ya Msingi katika Mtaala wa Kiumilisi (CBC) ambayo wanafunzi

watajiunga nayo baada ya kumaliza Chekechea, Shule ya Msingi na Shule ya Junia. Lengo kuu la Daraja ya juu ya shule za upili

ni kuwapa wanafunzi uzoefu wa awali wa chuo kikuu au taaluma, ambapo wanafunzi wanapata fursa ya kuchagua mielekeo na

nyanja wanazovutiwa nazo na walizoonyesha uwezo katika viwango vya awali. Daraja ya juu ya shule za upili inajumuisha miaka

mitatu ya masomo kwa wanafunzi walio kati ya umri wa miaka 16 -18 na huweka msingi wa elimu ya juu zaidi, mafunzo ya

kitaaluma na ulimwengu wa kazi. Katika ruwaza ya Mtaala wa Kiumilisi, wanafunzi watakaohitimu katika kiwango hiki

wanatarajiwa kuwa raia waliohusishwa, waliowezeshwa na waadilifu na walio tayari kushiriki katika maendeleo ya kijamii na

kiuchumi ya taifa.

Katika kiwango hiki, wanafunzi watajifunza masomo saba (7) kama ilivyopendekezwa na Kamati ya Rais ya Mageuzi ya Elimu

(PWPER, 2023). Masomo haya yanajumuisha masomo manne ya lazima ambayo ni: English, Kiswahili, Community Service

Learning (CSL) na Physical Education (PE).

Wanafunzi watachagua masomo mengine matatu kulingana na chaguo la taaluma, vipaji, mapendeleo yao kwa somo fulani, na

haiba zao, wakielekezwa na mwalimu anayehusika na uelekezaji wa kitaaluma wa Daraja ya juu ya shule za upili.

vi

MATOKEO YA KIJUMLA YA DARAJA YA JUU YA SHULE ZA UPILI

Kufikia mwisho wa daraja ya juu ya shule za upili, mwanafunzi aweze:

1. Kuwasiliana ipasavyo na kutumia teknolojia ya habari na mawasiliano katika miktadha mbalimbali,

2. Kutumia maarifa ya kihisabati, kimantiki na uwazaji kina katika utatuzi wa matatizo,

3. Kutumia maarifa ya kimsingi ya utafiti na ya kisayansi kuingiliana na mazingira yake na kutatua matatizo mbalimbali,

4. Kutumia vizuri vipaji mbalimbali kwa ajili ya burudani, kujiendeleza kitaaluma, kielimu pamoja na kimafunzo,

5. Kudumisha tunu za kitaifa, kimaadili na kidini katika maisha ya kila siku,

6. Kutumia na kuendeleza mikakati ya utunzaji wa kiafya katika maisha ya kila siku,

7. Kulinda, kuhifadhi na kuboresha mazingira kwa ajili ya uendelevu,

8. Kudhihirisha uraia wa kitaifa na wa kimataifa kwa ajili ya utangamano wa kidugu,

9. Kuonyesha uthamini wa tofauti za watu na tamaduni,

10. Kuonyesha uwajibikaji katika kukabiliana na masuala mtambuko.

KAULI KIINI

Somo la Kiswahili katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za Upili linamwandaa mwanafunzi kuwa mtumiaji mweledi wa lugha ya

Kiswahili katika mazingira na miktadha mbalimbali ya kijamii kwa kuongozwa na kanuni za ufasaha wa lugha. Ufasaha huu

unajengwa kwa kushiriki katika shughuli mbalimbali za ujifunzaji zinazokuza stadi za kusikiliza, kuzungumza, kusoma na

kuandika, pamoja na matumizi ya lugha. Kwa kushiriki shughuli hizi, mwanafunzi anapata umilisi wa kimawasiliano ambao

utamwezesha kuchangamkia lugha ya Kiswahili pamoja na utamaduni wa Kiafrika.

Katiba ya Kenya 2010, imekipa Kiswahili hadhi ya lugha rasmi na ya taifa sambamba na Kiingereza. Hadhi hii imekifanya

Kiswahili kutumika katika mawanda mapana, ukiwemo ulimwengu wa ajira. Somo la Kiswahili katika Daraja ya Juu ya Shule za

Upili linamwandaa mwanafunzi kushiriki katika mawanda haya kwa kumwekea msingi mzuri wa usomi katika somo la Kiswahii

huku likimtayarisha kwa ajili ya ajira, na maisha ya ulimwengu mpana unaohitaji maarifa mapevu ya mawasiliano na utatuzi wa

matatizo. Kupitia somo la Kiswahili, mwanafunzi ataweza kupata stadi za - karne ya ishirini na moja na kumwezesha kuwa raia

wa ulimwengu mpana. Hivyo basi, mwanafunzi wa somo la Kiswahili katika kiwango hiki anaandaliwa kuwa mhimili muhimu

katika ulimwengu wa Kiswahili unaozidi kupanuka na kupata hadhi mpya kila uchao. Anaandaliwa kuweza kutumia Kiswahili

ipasavyo katika kutekeleza majukumu ya taaluma atakayoichagua.

MATOKEO YA KIJUMLA YA SOMO LA KISWAHILI KATIKA DARAJA YA JUU YA SHULE ZA UPILI

Kufikia mwisho wa Daraja ya juu ya Shule za Upili, mwanafunzi aweze:

1. Kusikiliza kwa makini na kuitikia ipasavyo kwa Kiswahili katika miktadha mbalimbali ya mawasiliano,

2. Kujieleza ipasavyo kimazungumzo na kimaandishi kwa kuzingatia kanuni za lugha ya Kiswahili,

3. Kuwasiliana ipasavyo katika miktadha mbalimbali ya kijamii,

4. Kusoma kwa ufasaha na kufasiri matini mbalimbali zilizochapishwa na za kidijitali ili kupata ujumbe,

5. Kutumia teknolojia ipasavyo katika ujifunzaji na mawasiliano ili kukuza ujuzi wa kidijitali,

6. Kutumia maadili yanayohitajika maishani kupitia stadi za lugha ya Kiswahili,

7. Kuonea fahari lugha ya Kiswahili kama lugha rasmi, ya taifa na kimataifa.

Umilisi wa Kimsingi Unaokuzwa:

● Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: Mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutambua miktadha ambapo kusikiliza kwa

kuhakiki hutokea katika jamii.

● Kujiamini: Mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuwawasilishia wenzake tahakiki aliyoiandika ili wamtolee maoni.

● Ujuzi wa kidijitali: Mwanafunzi anapotalii mtandao salama kutafiti sifa za kusikiliza kwa kuhakiki. Pia, anapoandika

tahakiki katika kifaa cha kidijitali.

● Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: Mwanafunzi anapotumia kanuni za kusikiliza kwa kuhakiki kutenga hoja halisi na

ufafanuzi wazo.

● Ubunifu: Mwanafunzi anapoandika tahakiki kutokana na ujumbe aliopata katika matini semwa aliyosikiliza.

Maadili:

● Uwajibikaji: Mwanafunzi anapozingatia hatua za kiusalama anaposakura mtandaoni. Pia, anaposhiriki kikamilifu katika

shughuli za ujifunzaji.

● Heshima: Mwanafunzi anapokubali maoni na tathmini ya wenzake kuhusu tahakiki yake.

● Umoja: Mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kujadili kanuni za kusikiliza kwa kuhakiki na kuziandika kwenye chati.

● Upendo: Mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni yao kuhusu tahakiki yake.

Masuala Mtambuko:

● Suala la afya: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza na kuhakiki matini kuhusu matumizi yafaayo ya dawa.

● Mahusiano ya kijamii: Mwanafunzi anapotumia njia zifaazo kuafikiana na wenzake wenye mitazamo tofauti, uhusiano

bora unajengeka.

● Ujitambuaji: Mwanafunzi anapotambua uwezo na udhaifu wake katika kutunga tahakiki kutoka matini ya kusikiliza kwa

kuhakiki huku akizingatia vipengele vifaavyo.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships that are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. In the wake of rapid modernisation, there is bound to be a silent social revolution.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities required to support a

growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy that needs an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

ii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equality and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iii

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

vi

ESSENCE STATEMENT

The study of Literature in Senior School builds upon the foundational language and literary skills acquired at Junior School under

the integrated approach. This stage marks a significant transition, where learners begin to engage with more complex literary texts

and themes that reflect societal values, human experiences, and diverse cultures. As a pre-career stage, Senior School offers

learners the opportunity to refine their communication skills, critical thinking, empathy, and creativity—attributes that are vital

across numerous professional fields. Literature, therefore, becomes a key discipline in nurturing learners who are not only

academically competent but also socially aware and ethically grounded.

In line with CBC principles, the teaching and learning of Literature in Senior School is crafted to be learner-centred and activity- based, promoting autonomy and discovery. Learners are encouraged to take ownership of their learning through guided reading,

group discussions, dramatisation, performance, and fieldwork projects and activities such as theatre visits and storytelling sessions.

Emphasis is placed on “learning to learn,” where students develop metacognitive skills, reflective habits, and the ability to apply

literary knowledge in varied contexts. Writing remains a core component, with learners engaging in creative and analytical writing

tasks that foster expression, interpretation, and critique. Assessment is continuous and performance-based, allowing for holistic

development.

By the time learners exit Senior School, they should demonstrate a well-rounded profile that includes advanced communication

skills, cultural literacy, ethical sensitivity, and creative expression. These competencies prepare them not only for tertiary education

but also for the dynamic world of work. Literature opens pathways to a range of careers such as teaching, journalism, publishing,

theatre arts, law, media, and communication. Moreover, the study of Literature equips learners with the soft skills and emotional

intelligence required in any professional setting, fostering adaptable, thoughtful, and articulate individuals ready to contribute

meaningfully to society.

vii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR LITERATURE IN ENGLISH

By the end of the course, the learner should be able to:

1. Critically analyse literary texts and relate them to real life experiences.

2. Apply literary terms and devices effectively in school and real life.

3. Develop critical thinking skills for problem solving.

4. Apply digital literacy skills to enhance the learning, production and enjoyment of literature.

5. Appreciate skills to understand human nature and emotions as brought out in literature and real life.

6. Develop research skills for lifelong learning of literature.

7. Acquire skills for the creation, performance and preservation of literature for study, self-expression, enjoyment and for the

good of society.

8. Appreciate literature in its various forms and relate it to human experiences and values.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They

must be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of

nationhood by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster

patriotism, and to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid

modernisation. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required

to support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya

recognizes the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be

part of this development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will

prepare our young people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help

children to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound

moral values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities

and corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the

contemporary society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must

follow rapid development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

In Senior School, Biology builds on the foundational knowledge and scientific skills acquired in Integrated Science in Junior

School. At this level, learners deepen their understanding of the structure and functions of living organisms, their life processes,

interaction within the ecosystems, and the continuity of life through reproduction and inheritance. The subject focuses on equipping

learners with skills in observation, inquiry, critical thinking, and scientific reasoning. Emphasis is laid on understanding the

relevance of Biology in everyday life and its role in addressing real-world issues such as health, food security, and environmental

conservation.

Learning in Biology will focus on practical activities, experiments, and scientific investigations. Learners will engage in research,

data analysis, and effective communication of findings. The approach will foster the development of core competencies like

collaborative learning, critical thinking and problem-solving and also learning to learn where the learners will apply the biological

concepts to new situations and ensure there is holistic development of the learner. This will not only equip learners for higher

learning and the world of work but also nature responsible citizenship.

Biology will open up diverse career pathways for learners, especially in fields related to health, agriculture, environmental

management, and research. The subject lays a solid foundation for professions such as medicine, nursing, veterinary science,

biotechnology, microbiology, environmental science, public health, and forensic science. It also supports innovation and

entrepreneurship in areas like pharmaceuticals, food technology, and conservation, thereby contributing to Kenya’s socio- economic development and global competitiveness.

viii

BIOLOGY GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of the course the learner should be able to:

1. develop relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes for further education and training in Biology related scientific fields,

2. demonstrate an understanding of interrelationships among humans, other organisms and their environment and apply the

knowledge to conserve nature,

3. describe features of various groups of living organisms and identify unknown organisms using simple biological keys,

4. apply the knowledge gained on human body systems and functions to improve the quality of life for self and the

community while enhancing healthy living,

5. design and conduct practical activities and projects that will enable them to understand biological concepts,

6. demonstrate relevant technical skills and scientific knowledge necessary for socio-economic development,

7. demonstrate resourcefulness in designing projects necessary for community service learning,

8. communicate biological information in a precise, clear and logical manner,

9. apply knowledge of plant and animal structure and functions to industrialization, innovation and sustainability of life,

10. use the knowledge gained to make informed decisions about scientifically-based personal and societal issues to solve

emerging issues in health and environment.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iv

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

v

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Chemistry is introduced to learners at the Senior School level as a continuation of the foundational concepts covered under

Integrated Science in Junior School. At this level, learners explore the composition, properties, transformations, and behavioural

changes of matter, which make up the physical world around them. The subject aims to build learners’ understanding of scientific

principles with a strong focus on problem-solving and real-life applications. Learners will gain foundational competencies in

scientific reasoning, critical thinking and science process skills that are essential in the fields of Science and Technology.

Learning in Chemistry is centred on practical experiences and scientific inquiry to help learners make meaningful connections

between theory and real-world applications. The curriculum employs methods such as Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL), Project- Based Learning (PBL), Problem-Based Learning, fieldwork, and excursions to promote active engagement and deep

understanding. Emphasis is placed on the correct use of scientific terminology, chemical equations, and the International Union of

Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) system of nomenclature, ensuring that learners acquire the necessary skills to interpret and

apply scientific concepts accurately.

By acquiring foundational knowledge and skills in Chemistry, learners are well-prepared for tertiary education in a wide range of

fields such as medicine, pharmacy, engineering, agriculture, and environmental science. The competencies developed also position

them for opportunities in industrial, research, and technical careers.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Acquire scientific knowledge, skills, values and attitudes for everyday use, and further education and training;

2. Conduct a range of scientific investigations, including collection of qualitative and quantitative data, analysis and

interpretation of results;

3. Use scientific language in the study of Chemistry;

4. Develop skills and logical thinking in carrying out project work, field work and excursions, where chemistry can be

appreciated on a larger scale;
