NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development

in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Mathematics plays an important role in society through developing the learners’ critical, creative and logical reasoning, for

purposes of acquisition of competencies necessary for problem solving in day to day life. It is applied in Social Sciences, Arts and

Sports Science and Science, Technology, Engineering (STEM) pathways. Further, Mathematics is useful in computations,

measurements, and the study of geometry as well as some aspects of the earth to appreciate different time zones in the world. In

addition, Statistics and Probability are critical in research and in understanding of different population dynamics and

characteristics. Key pertinent issues such as financial literacy, citizenship and education for sustainable development as well as

values are integrated into Mathematics to improve the social and economic wellbeing of the individual and the society.

In Senior School, Mathematics builds on the competencies acquired by the learner from Junior school. It enhances the learner's

skills in using mathematics effectively, efficiently and critically to make informed decisions including the choice of projects for

experiential learning. The subject also provides opportunities to students to prepare for post-school options of further training in

careers such as medical fields, engineering, researchers, physicists, actuarial scientists as well as entrepreneurship.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of the course the learner should be able to:

a) Develop numerical computational skills, concepts and competencies for continuous learning and application of Mathematics,

b) Develop critical and creative thinking, logical reasoning, and communication skills for problem solving,

c) Use Mathematical concepts and skills to support other learning areas for further training, research and career development,

d) Build confidence and interest in Mathematics for lifelong learning,

e) Evaluate and make financial decisions and transactions in real life situations,

f) Model geometric structures in real life situations,

g) Collect, analyze and present data to inform and solve problems in real life situations,

h) Use digital technologies for Mathematical manipulations, explorations and innovations, and for further learning,

i) Appreciate the aesthetic value of Mathematics in different contexts.

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead

to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compul`sory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Essential Mathematics in Senior School builds on and deepens the competencies acquired by the learner from Junior school. It plays a pivotal

role in developing the learner’s computational abilities as well as critical thinking and problem solving skills. Specifically, the subject focuses

on numbers and algebra as foundation to the course in developing numerical and algebraic thinking. It also includes measurements of different

quantities, particularly commercial arithmetic which is important for acquisition and application of financial literacy in real life. Further, some

concepts in geometry are included since they are useful in spatial relations as well as navigational skills while Statistics and Probability are

critical in research and in understanding different population dynamics and phenomena that are useful in solving problems in day to day life.

This Mathematics curriculum has explicitly suggested learning activities that focus on the mathematical process skills of problem solving,

communication, connection, collaboration and reasoning as core to acquisition of the desirable competencies. Similarly, for holistic

development and wellbeing of learners Pertinent and Contemporary Issues such as Life Skills, Citizenship and Education for Sustainable

Development as well as Values are integrated into this Mathematics course.

Essential Mathematics is crucial in supporting and enhancing acquisition of knowledge and skills in other subjects. Further, it is critical in

determining career choices in the fields of Social Sciences, Arts, Sports, vocational and humanities. Careers in areas such as media, hospitality

industry, guidance and counseling, sole proprietorship, sports management, coaching, refereeing, journalism and photography will benefit

from this Mathematics. More importantly, its aesthetic and utility value in day to day activities will contribute to an informed numerate

citizenry.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of the course the learner should be able to:

1. Acquire numerical computational skills, concepts and competencies for continuous learning and application of mathematical skills in

real life,

2. Apply measurement skills of different quantities used in daily activities,

3. Evaluate and make financial decisions and transactions in real-life situations,

4. Collect, analyse and represent data for informed decision-making in real-life situations,

5. Use mathematical concepts and skills to support other learning subjects for further training, research and career development,

6. Develop confidence and interest in mathematics as well as the coherence, utility and aesthetic nature of the subject for lifelong learning,

7. Apply critical and creative thinking, logical reasoning and analytical skills for problem-solving,

8. Use digital technology in computations, explorations, innovations, navigational skills and for further learning,

9. Demonstrate appropriate responsiveness to Pertinent and Contemporary Issues in the community and promote values for peaceful

coexistence.

STRANDS

The Essential Mathematics curriculum has 3 strands namely:

1. Numbers and Algebra,

2. Measurements and Geometry; and

3. Statistics and Probability.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures, and

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

General Science at Senior School utilises scientific and technological knowledge which builds on the foundational concepts

acquired from Integrated Science at Junior School. The learning area seeks to equip learners with functional investigative and

application skills relating to life science. It focuses on biological, physical and chemical phenomena of life. It also deals with

society’s need to understand how the physical environment works in order to benefit from it and responsibly care for it. It is

intended to develop competencies in the learner to solve societal and technological problems while taking care of the environment.

Some of the skills relevant to the study of General Science include; classifying, communicating, measuring, designing an

investigation, drawing and evaluating conclusions to cultivate competencies in responsible citizenship, sustainable environmental

management, and socio-economic development.

The learning area emphasises experiential learning and scientific inquiry to bridge concept with real-life application. The learner

will need to formulate models, make observations, hypothesise, identify and control variables, interpret data and make inferences

based on scientific evidence for meaningful learning experiences. The curriculum design adopts approaches such as Inquiry-Based

Learning (IBL), Project-Based Learning (PBL), Problem-Based Learning (PBL), fieldwork and excursions to enhance active

engagement and understanding of the concepts. It aims to develop learners' problem-solving and reflective thinking skills to

address real-life challenges.

The concepts and skills are crucial for success in various fields of study, employment or world of work. Consequently, studying

General Science provides an opportunity and foundation for the learner to explore and excel in specialist fields such as sports and

talent based areas, applied science courses, environmental conservation, common therapeutic treatments and health-related careers.

In this regard, the learning area plays an increasingly important role in the lives of learners owing to the influence on scientific

and technological development, which are necessary for the country’s economic growth and the social wellbeing of its people.

a) Acquire functional investigative and application skills relating to life science to enhance appreciation of the environment.

b) Use appropriate instruments to carry out basic science process skills.

c) Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve human problems.

d) Develop critical thinking skills through basic science processes and research in addressing pertinent & contemporary issues

in the society.

e) Apply scientific and technological skills to enhance innovations and entrepreneurship for sustainable development.

f) Use competencies and values to promote local and global citizenship for harmonious coexistence and appreciation of

biodiversity.

g) Acquire knowledge, skills and attitudes to enhance exploitation of individual talents for leisure, self -fulfilment, career

growth and for further education and training.

h) Appreciate the use of effective communication and utilisation of information in scientific advancement.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able to

live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, which enable them to live together in harmony and foster patriotism in

order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth

progress of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid

modernisation. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of

individual talents and personality. It should help children to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual

development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instill in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the

youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/

pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners

exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of

the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

School career teacher.

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Physics is a body of knowledge examining the theories, principles and laws that regulate natural occurrences seen in the physical

world. In Senior School, physics expands on the skills developed during Junior School in the Integrated Science learning area. In

Kenya's Vision 2030 and in the sessional papers No. 1 of 2005 and No. 1 of 2019, the significance of science, technology, and

innovation has been highlighted for developing human capital via education and training. Physics is a crucial component of the

STEM disciplines within the Basic Education Curriculum Framework. It utilises a scientific method of research focusing on an

experimental approach to inquiry, improving comprehension of basic scientific concepts and principles. This results in gaining

knowledge, scientific methods, practical abilities, fostering positive attitudes and values through precise and accurate scientific

practices.

Physics provides the learner with opportunities to develop competencies by empowering them to be creative and innovative,

leading to independent approaches in problem solving and management of their environment. It also prepares learners for further

training and the world of work by providing careers in STEM-related pathways. Physics will include concepts in mechanics and

thermal physics, waves and optics, electricity and magnetism, environmental and space physics. The content will be anchored on

Kolb Theory of Experiential Learning and Constructivism Theory for teaching and learning.

The content gives the foundations for understanding interaction between objects and energy in the physical world, understanding

essential phenomena in nature and technology, including sound, light, vision and modern communication systems, forces that

underpin modern technology and natural phenomena, from electric circuits to electromagnetic waves and even how the universe

functions. It also enhances understanding of the physical processes governing Earth's environment and space weather, which

impact technology, climate and life on our planet. The subject will provide opportunities for learners to prepare for post-school

further training in but not limited to careers such as engineering, research physicist, physics educators, space weather scientists,

atmospheric or climate modelers and remote sensing scientists or earth observation specialists.

SUBJECT LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School the learner should be able to:

1. Relate Physics to technology and society to enhance the learner’s appreciation of the physical environment.

2. Develop science process skills among learners through the use of appropriate instruments as they discover and explain the

order of the physical environment.

3. Apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve human problems.

4. Develop capacity for critical thinking through basic scientific skills and research in addressing pertinent and contemporary

issues affecting the society.

5. Apply the principles of Physics for enhancement of innovations and entrepreneurial skills for development.

6. Use relevant skills and values to promote local and global citizenship for harmonious coexistence and appreciation of

diversity in people.

7. Acquire adequate knowledge, skills, values and attitudes to enhance exploitation of individual talents for leisure, self- fulfillment, career growth, and for further education and training.

8. Apply acquired knowledge, skills, values, and attitudes for effective communication and utilisation of information in

technological advancement.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

Kenya’s people belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect which enable them to live together in harmony and foster

patriotism in order to make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution following in the wake of rapid

modernization. Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy which is in need of an adequate and

relevant domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health in order for them to avoid indulging in activities that will

lead to physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It

should lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after

the Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre- tertiary/university/ pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they

shall have demonstrated interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners

generally in the 16-18 years age bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of

work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate

in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the

Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM

pathways). The learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance

by the Senior School career teacher.

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Christian Religious Education is the study of God's self-revelation to humankind through personal experiences, the scriptures, the

life and Ministry of Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit. The concepts taught in this grade build on what was learned in Grade 11.

Christian Religious Education is anchored in the National Goal of Education number 4, which states that education should promote

sound moral and religious values. The values include chastity, love, respect, obedience, kindness, patience, integrity, and

responsibility. The skills include praying, meditating on scriptures, interpreting scriptures, leadership skills, self-awareness, self- esteem, self-control, assertiveness and decision-making. The ultimate goal of Christian Religious Education is to produce a learner

who is God fearing, ethical, innovative, and a critical thinker able to participate in the global platform.

After Senior School the subject will facilitate the learner to further their education in various careers such as law, Christian

ministry, teaching, counselling, administration, authorship, charity work, child & youth worker, clergy, chaplain, pastoral

counsellor, community centre director, community developer, diplomat, entrepreneur, foreign service worker, lobbyist, media

correspondent, mediator, missionary, non-profit administrator, religious rights advocate, researcher or a social service worker.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Utilise principles of good stewardship as they perform tasks at home, school, and church.

2. Interpret teachings in the Holy Bible for moral, spiritual, character development and growth.

3. Apply the teachings of Jesus Christ in their daily interactions to promote social equality and responsibility.

4. Analyse contemporary social and moral issues to make informed ethical decisions.

5. Manipulate research and digital literacy skills in learning Christian Religious Education.

6. Develop requisite knowledge, skills, values, and attitudes to further their studies in various career fields.

7. Create ingenuities using 21st-century skills to compete in the global platform.

8. Appreciate the church's role in promoting spiritual transformation and good citizens

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and to

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships, which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead

the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Hindu Religious Education (HRE) at Senior School level builds on knowledge, skills, attitudes and values that were acquired,

developed and nurtured in the learner at Junior School level. The Hindu Religious Education curriculum will enable the learner to

forge their own personal identity. Emphasis will be placed on aspects that mould them to appreciate their own and others’ religious

beliefs, values and cultural practices for global citizenship.

The HRE curriculum involves the study of Paramatma for strengthening the learner’s understanding and beliefs in the

(Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist and Sikh) faiths, the Historical development of the four faiths, core beliefs, development of the

Scriptures for firm grounding in the four faiths, Principles of Dharma and the Law of Karma. The curriculum is enriched with

practical simulations that will empower the learner to live the faith and manage challenges in life effectively. The acquired

knowledge, developed skills, formed attitude and nurtured values will help the learner to make informed choices in their careers

and future endeavours.

Through a value based transformative approach, the learner will be guided to develop a sense of identity, belonging and a self- inquiry approach about physical, psychosocial, ethical and spiritual faculties. This is in line with relevant constructivist learning

theoretical approaches such as Vygotsky’s Theory of Learning, Erik Erikson’s Stages of Psychosocial Development, Kolb’s

Experiential Learning and Roger’s Humanism’s learning.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of the Senior School level, the learner should be able to:

1. interpret concepts on the Manifestations of Paramatma for appropriate response in his/her relationship with the ultimate and

other creations as guided by the Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh faiths

2. examine the development of the Scriptures in the four faiths for instilling values and desirable behaviour in daily interactions

3. apply the Principles of Dharma for a righteous living

4. analyse the Law of Karma for decision making in daily life

5. acknowledge the relevance of Cultural Practices in the four faiths for enhancing career choices

6. appreciate cultural and religious Heritage for self-identity and posterity

7. discuss the Historical Development of the four faiths for harmonious coexistence

8. utilise Digital Literacy skills for communication and inclusive learning.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development

in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Islamic Religious Education (IRE) learning area aims at equipping learners with knowledge, skills, attitudes and moral values that

enable them to perform their role as vicegerents of Allah (S.W.T.) responsibly. The Qur’an and the Sunnah (practices of Prophet

Muhammad (S.A.W)) form one of the key frameworks in facilitating learning in this area.

The transition from Junior School to Senior School marks an important step in a learner’s academic journey bringing greater

responsibility and deeper understanding of IRE. Islamic Religious Education in Junior School laid foundation on Ulumul Qur’an,

Ulumul Hadith, Pillars of Iman, Devotional acts, aspects of moral teaching and prohibitions in Islam, social relationship and

Islamic heritage and civilisation. The skills acquired at this level were intrapersonal and interpersonal skills, communication skills

and investigative skills.

As learners progress to Senior School the skills will be amplified with an in-depth analysis on Qur’an and Hadith, Fiqh and

Muamalat (Jurisprudence and Social Relationships), Akhlaq (Moral Teachings) and Islamic History and Civilization. This will be

achieved through a learner centred approach which includes discussion, simulation and carrying out projects.

Learners interested in this learning area may aspire for career paths as educationists, scholars in Islamic Studies, law, judicial

officers, chaplains, and spiritual leaders, diplomats, journalism among others.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior Secondary, the learner should be able to:

1. develop understanding and apply the teachings of the Qur’an and Hadith for guidance

2. uphold Islamic beliefs and practices, perform devotional acts to fulfil Allah (S.W.T.)’s commandments for holistic human

growth and sustainable use of resources

3. develop positive inter-personal relationships guided by Islamic ethos for a harmonious society

4. practise Islamic virtues and morals for an upright society and appreciate religious diversity for tolerance and social cohesion

5. demonstrate understanding and application of Islamic law in maintenance of peace and social order in the society

viii

6. apply Islamic teachings to guide individuals to make positive contribution to social, political and economic developments in

the society

7. demonstrate appreciation of the contribution of Islamic culture to world civilisation and heritage and the role of technology

in facilitating learning of Islamic Religious Education.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iv

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development

in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

v

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Aviation explores the dynamic world of flight and introduces the learner to the science and technology of aircraft and aerospace.

It builds on the foundational concepts introduced in Pre-Technical Studies at Junior School and is aligned to the Technical Studies

track of the Science Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) pathway.

The subject equips learners with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills in aviation safety, aircraft construction, flight and

airport operations. Through practical hands-on experiences, project-based learning, simulations, engaging with real-world

applications and emerging technologies, learners will develop competencies in designing, constructing and maintaining basic

aircraft structures and systems, applying aviation safety standards, conducting flight and airport operations and appreciating

aviation's impact on society and the environment.

Upon completion, learners will be prepared to transition into the world of work as apprentices or pursue further studies in aviation

and related fields. The subject opens up to careers in fields such as aircraft maintenance, flight and airport operations, aviation

safety and aviation entrepreneurship. Learners may also progress to technical and vocational education and training (TVET)

institutions, aviation colleges, or university-level programs in piloting, aeronautical engineering, flight and airport operations or

aviation management.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Demonstrate understanding of aviation theories, concepts, principles and operations.

2. Apply safety practices and procedures in aviation environments.

3. Evaluate weather, human and environmental factors in relation to flight operations.

4. Read, interpret and use aircraft related drawings.

5. Apply financial and consumer literacy skills in aviation entrepreneurship.

6. Apply emerging technologies and environmentally sustainable practices in aviation.

7. Collaborate effectively with others when executing aviation tasks related to aviation.

ix

8. Explore career opportunities in the aviation industry.
