NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony and foster patriotism, and to

make a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships, which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognises

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of individual talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system that provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead

the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

As a country with a robust construction industry coupled with a rapid growth in human population and need for descent housing,

Kenya needs qualified personnel equipped with knowledge, skills, and desired attitudes in building construction processes

especially at the operative level.

The introduction of Building Construction as a technical and engineering studies subject at Senior School shall prepare learners to

acquire knowledge, develop technical skills and form positive attitudes in masonry, plumbing, concreting, and other trades in

building construction. It builds on competencies acquired in Pre-Technical Studies at Junior School. It is anchored on Sessional

Papers No. 1 of 2005 and No. 1 of 2019 which recommended the promotion of technical and vocational education with an emphasis

on Science, Technology and Innovation (ST&I) in the school curriculum.

The course has been designed in such a way as to cater for the needs of students who wish to further their education as well as

those who wish to exit Senior School to the world of work. For students who wish to go on to higher levels of education and

training in Technical Universities, National Polytechnics, Technical and Vocational Colleges, or Vocational Training Centres, it

provides adequate knowledge and skills for success at such levels. Students who wish to terminate their course at Senior School

would also have had adequate level of skills and knowledge in building resources, building construction processes, and financial

literacy that will enable them get into the world of work.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of the Senior School, the learner should be able to:

a) select a preferred career in building construction,

b) draw and interpret working drawings,

c) carry out masonry works,

d) carry out concreting works for simple buildings,

e) install and maintain plumbing systems,

f) provide for and observe safety on a building construction site,

g) care for and maintain construction plant, tools, and equipment,

h) prepare quantities for simple building projects, and

i) develop financial literacy for management of building construction projects.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make

a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children

to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iv

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

v

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Electricity is an essential form of energy in the modern world. The study of Electricity at senior school level equips learners with

foundational knowledge and skills that are essential for understanding and harnessing electrical energy in daily life, industry, and

emerging technologies. This justifies the need to offer Electricity as a subject in Senior School to help orient learners towards the

development of a skilled workforce in electrical technology. The subject builds on the basic concepts introduced in Junior School

Integrated Science and Pre-Technical Studies, providing a deeper and more structured understanding that supports both academic

progression and practical application.

Electricity as a subject forms part of the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) pathway at the senior school

level. STEM has been prioritised in Kenya Vision 2030, as well as in Sessional Paper No. 1 of 2019, as pivotal to the development

of science, technology, and innovation for human capital development. In this subject, learners engage with theoretical concepts,

practical investigations, and hands-on skills in the handling of electric circuits, electrical and electronic machines, electrical

installation, and associated safety practices.

The subject is designed to provide learners with knowledge, practical skills, attitudes, and values that will enable them to use

electricity and electrical appliances competently and safely. It also prepares learners to pursue further studies in colleges and other

vocational pathways in fields such as electrical power engineering, mechatronic engineering, telecommunication engineering,

control engineering, and electronic engineering, among others, or to enter the world of work as an electrical apprentice.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Observe personal safety, safety of tools, equipment and machines in the practice of electrical technology works.

2. Analyse, design, and construct electric circuits.

3. Troubleshoot and fix faults in electrical and electronic systems.

4. Apply appropriate communication skills across varied settings and audiences in interpretation of electrical technology works.

5. Practice good citizenship in waste management and ethical use of electronic and electrical technologies.

6. Adhere to the established standards and regulations in electrical technology to uphold professional and ethical practices.

7. Utilise acquired skills, knowledge and attitude for career growth and further education and training in electrical technology.

8. Appreciate electrical technology in the socio-economic development of the country.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make

a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children

to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after

the Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre- tertiary/university/ pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they

shall have demonstrated interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners

generally in the 16-18 years age bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of

work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate

in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the

Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM

pathways). The learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance

by the Senior School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

At the Junior School level, learners are introduced to foundational concepts in Integrated Science, Pre-technical Studies and

Agriculture. These early experiences nurture awareness of aquatic ecosystems and natural resource conservation. As learners

transition into Senior School, Marine and Fisheries Technology builds upon this foundation by deepening their understanding and

introducing more specialised knowledge and technical skills related to fisheries, marine ecosystems and maritime operations.

The curriculum is therefore designed to stimulate learners’ interest in the fisheries sectors and equip them with essential knowledge,

practical skills, positive attitudes and values for participation in both local and international fisheries-related careers. fish biology

and ecology, aquaculture, capture fisheries, fish production, conservation, the sustainable development of the fisheries industry,

maritime operations and seamanship, effects of weather and changing climatic conditions on marine and fisheries activities, safety

of humans and equipment undertaking marine activities, and fishery by-products and their industrial uses.

By involving learners in experiential and learner-centered activities through classroom instruction, practical work, field trips,

projects and simulations, this subject aims to increase their interest and involvement in the fishing industry. Learners will engage

in activities like species identification, managing fishponds, using fishing gear, processing and preservation methods, applying

fisheries laws, practicing safety and survival techniques and improvising solutions in maritime operations. The curriculum

emphasises competency acquisition, practical orientation, career pathways and responsibility toward marine conservation and

sustainable use of aquatic resources.

In blending theory and practice, learners are prepared for future academic training or immediate entry into the workforce, while

being empowered to contribute meaningfully to Kenya’s growing blue economy and the global fisheries industry. Learning in this

subject supports a wide range of career opportunities, including Fisheries Officer, Marine Biologist, Aquaculture Technician, Fish

Farm Manager, Environmental Conservationist, Marine Engineer, Fish Processing Technologist, Fisheries Economist, Coastal and

Marine Resource Manager, Maritime Safety Officer, Policy Analyst (Marine and Fisheries) and an entrepreneur in aquaculture or

fish processing. In this way, the curriculum equips learners not only with the technical skills and knowledge for sustainable marine

and freshwater resource management but also with the positive attitudes, values and practical experience to innovate, lead, and

thrive in the dynamic fisheries and maritime sectors locally and globally.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

a) Acquire knowledge, skills and attitudes on fish biology, culture and management of marine and freshwater resources.

b) Design and operate simple fish production systems and apply appropriate fishing techniques and equipment.

c) Comprehend and respect laws, policies and regulations governing fisheries

d) Identify potential business opportunities in the fisheries sector.

e) Demonstrate basic maritime scientific skills.

f) Identify potential hazards and safety requirements for humans and equipment during marine operations.

g) Analyse the effects of weather patterns and changing climatic conditions on fisheries and other marine activities.

h) Apply safety and survival techniques during marine operations for both humans and equipment.

i) Demonstrate practical skills in using and processing fishery by-products for industrial and commercial purposes

j) Appreciate the importance of fisheries and marine resources in the socio-economic development in Kenya.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be able

to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by resolving

conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a positive

contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of a

rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

v

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid development

in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

vi

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Media Technology in the Senior School curriculum builds upon foundational competencies developed in Junior School Pre-Technical Studies,

with an expanded focus on the dynamic interplay between media, information, communication, and the digital economy. Learners transition

from general exposure to technological tools to a more specialized engagement with content creation, media production, and immersive digital

environments. The subject introduces them to interactive platforms, emerging technologies, digital storytelling, and media entrepreneurship.

Rooted in the principles of the National ICT Policy (2019) and aligned with the UNESCO 2030 Sustainable Development Goals, the

curriculum emphasizes ethical digital citizenship, innovation, and critical engagement with media as both a tool and a transformative force in

society.

Learning in Media Technology is experiential and inquiry-based, with a strong emphasis on hands-on activities, project-based learning,

collaboration, and research. Learners are guided to think critically, work innovatively, and apply digital tools across various media formats.

They engage with real-world scenarios through simulations, prototyping, and problem-solving tasks that foster analytical and entrepreneurial

skills. Through iterative production processes and peer review, learners develop fluency in managing content, mastering digital tools, and

adapting to technological shifts. The progression of learning equips them with the competencies required for further education and for

responding to the evolving demands of the 21st-century knowledge economy.

Media Technology prepares learners for a broad spectrum of careers within the creative, digital, and communication sectors. Potential

pathways include digital content creation, film and television production, multimedia design, animation, journalism, advertising, game design,

virtual and augmented reality development, media research, and digital marketing. The subject also nurtures entrepreneurial capacity, enabling

learners to innovate within the digital economy and contribute meaningfully to Kenya’s creative industries and global media landscape. The

subject cultivates a generation of innovative, digitally literate, ethically grounded, and technologically adept industry-ready professionals

equipped to drive progress in their higher education and in the creative and digital industries both locally and globally.

6. Utilise media literacy skills to promote public health and conservation of the environment towards sustainable development.

7. Engage in local and international media as part of bringing about positive social change and coexistence in society.

8. Appreciate cultures and global outlook represented through media with respect.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be

able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a

positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of

a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernization. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfillment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/

pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners

exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of

the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The

learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior

School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Metalwork is one of the learning areas in the technical studies track of the Science Technology Engineering Mathematics (STEM)

pathway. It builds on the competencies acquired in Pre-Technical Studies, Integrated Science and other related learning areas at Junior

School. The subject equips the learner with knowledge, skills, values and competencies that are prerequisite for further training and

engagement in the world of work. Metalwork is a learning area that equips the learner with exploration, imagination, creativity,

innovation and hands-on skills through practical activities and projects.

The subject delivery emphasizes the use of learner centered approaches through varied facilitation, learning experiences and

resources. This approach entails both theory and practice, distributed equally throughout the subject. This is because the content is

developed from basic science and technology concepts to more advanced concepts based on the psychological development of the

learner. The strands include; Fundamentals of Metalwork, Tools and Materials, Sheet Metal Joining processes, Related Drawing and

Career Opportunities in Metalwork. These strands aim to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, innovation,

communication, digital literacy, and practical skills all considered essential in both personal life and the world of work.

This learning area is anchored in National Goals of Education No. 2 on providing the learners with the necessary skills and attitudes

for industrial development. It is aligned to the Kenya Vision 2030 which advocates for making education responsive to educational

needs. Metalwork is also in line with Sessional Paper No 1 of 2019 which recommends the promotion of technical and vocational

education with an emphasis on Science, Technology, and Innovation (ST&I) in the school curriculum.

Upon completing Senior School, learners may advance by enrolling in either a tertiary institution or university to further their studies

in engineering or technology-based courses. Alternatively, they can join related career opportunities on salaried or self-employment

terms.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Attain a firm foundation for the study of Metalwork, further training, and education.

2. Use knowledge and skills in drawing to design items that can be made using metals.

3. Use metals to fabricate items that can be used to solve problems in society.

4. Correctly select and use Metalworking tools and equipment for given tasks.

5. Carry out metal joining using the various metal joining processes.

6. Use acquired competencies in identifying business opportunities, set up, and ethically run an enterprise in a Metalworking

related field.

7. Prudently manage finances and create wealth using metallic materials.

8. Appreciate metal technology in technical and social economic development of the country.

9. Promote national and international consciousness fostering positive attitudes toward other people and nations.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must be

able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood by

resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make a

positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress of

a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation. Education

should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to support

a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant domestic

workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes the

rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this development

if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young people for these

changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children to

develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral values

and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides equal

educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and corporate

social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations. Education

should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the obligations and

responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to physical or

mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should lead the youth of

Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/

pre-career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners

exiting this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of

the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The

learner will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior

School career teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Power Mechanics as a subject build upon the competencies acquired in Pre-Technical studies at Junior School. At this level,

learners will deepen their understanding of mechanical principles, power systems and practical applications moving from basic

concepts to more complex and specialised ones.

The subject covers key content areas including; Fundamentals of power mechanics, Related drawing, Vehicle systems and

Engines. The transition emphasises enhanced critical thinking, problem-solving, and hands-on skills that prepare learners for

real-world technical challenges. Learner is expected to develop the core competencies and catch values outlined in the Basic

Education curriculum Framework (BECF). Pertinent and contemporary issues (PCIs) such as social economic, environmental

issues, citizenship education are mainstreamed in the learning experiences. Learning at this level is learner centred and formative

assessment is emphasised.

Upon completion of Senior School, competencies gained by learners in this subject will enable them transit into various post- secondary tertiary institutions such as Universities, National polytechnics, technical training institutes, Technical and vocational

centres or transit to the world of work.

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. Attain a firm foundation for career growth, further training and education in Power Mechanics related areas of study.

2. Utilise acquired Power Mechanics competencies to service and repair motor vehicle and machine systems.

3. Apply acquired drawing skills to interpret and communicate engineering designs using information and communication

technology where applicable.

4. Relate positively with members of the society during visits to the work environment.

5. Use acquired knowledge to identify business opportunities related to Power Mechanics

6. Appreciate the place of Power Mechanics in day-to-day life.

NATIONAL GOALS OF EDUCATION

Education in Kenya should:

1. Foster nationalism and patriotism and promote national unity.

The people of Kenya belong to different communities, races and religions, but these differences need not divide them. They must

be able to live and interact as Kenyans. It is a paramount duty of education to help young people acquire this sense of nationhood

by resolving conflicts and promoting positive attitudes of mutual respect, to live together in harmony, foster patriotism, and to make

a positive contribution to the life of the nation.

2. Promote the social, economic, technological, and industrial needs for national development.

Education should prepare the youth of the country to play an effective and productive role in the life of the nation.

a) Social Needs

Education in Kenya must prepare children for changes in attitudes and relationships which are necessary for the smooth progress

of a rapidly developing modern economy. There is bound to be a silent social revolution in the wake of rapid modernisation.

Education should assist our youth to adapt to this change.

b) Economic Needs

Education in Kenya should produce citizens with the skills, knowledge, expertise, and personal qualities that are required to

support a growing economy. Kenya is building up a modern and independent economy that requires an adequate and relevant

domestic workforce.

c) Technological and Industrial Needs

Education in Kenya should provide learners with the necessary skills and attitudes for industrial development. Kenya recognizes

the rapid industrial and technological changes taking place, especially in the developed world. We can only be part of this

development if our education system is deliberately focused on the knowledge, skills and attitudes that will prepare our young

people for these changing global trends.

3. Promote individual development and self-fulfilment.

Education should provide opportunities for the fullest development of an individual’s talents and personality. It should help children

to develop their potential interests and abilities. A vital aspect of individual development is the building of character.

iii

4. Promote sound moral and religious values.

Education should provide for the development of knowledge, skills and attitudes that will enhance the acquisition of sound moral

values and help children to grow up into self-disciplined, self-reliant, and integrated citizens.

5. Promote social equity and responsibility.

Education should promote social equality and foster a sense of social responsibility within an education system which provides

equal educational opportunities for all. It should give all children varied and challenging opportunities for collective activities and

corporate social service irrespective of gender, ability, or geographical environment.

6. Promote respect for and development of Kenya’s rich and varied cultures.

Education should instil in the youth of Kenya an understanding of past and present cultures and their valid place in the contemporary

society. Children should be able to blend the best of traditional values with the changing requirements that must follow rapid

development in order to build a stable and modern society.

7. Promote international consciousness and foster positive attitudes towards other nations.

Kenya is part of the international community. It is part of the complicated and interdependent network of peoples and nations.

Education should therefore lead the youth of the country to accept membership of this international community with all the

obligations and responsibilities, rights, and benefits that this membership entails.

8. Promote positive attitudes towards good health and environmental protection.

Education should inculcate in young people the value of good health for them to avoid indulging in activities that will lead to

physical or mental ill health. It should foster positive attitudes towards environmental development and conservation. It should

lead the youth of Kenya to appreciate the need for a healthy environment.

iv

THE SENIOR SCHOOL IN THE COMPETENCY BASED CURRICULUM

Senior School is the fourth level of Basic Education in the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) that the learner shall proceed to after the

Pre-Primary School, Primary School and Junior School levels. The essence of Senior School is to offer learners a pre-tertiary/university/ pre- career experience in which the learners have an opportunity to choose pathways, tracks and subjects where they shall have demonstrated

interest and/or potential at the earlier levels. Senior School comprises three years of education for learners generally in the 16-18 years age

bracket and lays the foundation for further education and training at the tertiary level and the world of work. In the CBC vision, learners exiting

this level are expected to be engaged, empowered and ethical citizens ready to participate in the socio-economic development of the nation.

At this level, the learner shall take seven (7) learning areas as recommended by the Presidential Working Party on Educational Reforms

(PWPER, 2023). These shall comprise four compulsory learning areas namely: English, Kiswahili, Essential Mathematics/Core

Mathematics and Community Service Learning (CSL). Learners will choose between Core Mathematics (for learners pursuing the Science

Technology Engineering and Mathematics Pathway) and Essential Mathematics (for learners pursuing the non-STEM pathways). The learner

will select three learning areas depending on their career choice, aptitude, interest and personality with guidance by the Senior School career

teacher.

LEARNING OUTCOMES FOR SENIOR SCHOOL

By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:

1. communicate effectively and utilise information and communication technology across varied contexts,

2. apply mathematical, logical and critical thinking skills for problem solving,

3. apply basic research and scientific skills to manipulate the environment and solve problems,

4. exploit individual talents for leisure, self-fulfilment, career growth, further education and training,

5. uphold national, moral and religious values and apply them in day-to-day life,

6. apply and promote health care strategies in day-to-day life,

7. protect, preserve and improve the environment for sustainability,

8. demonstrate active local and global citizenship for harmonious co-existence,

9. demonstrate appreciation of diversity in people and cultures,

10. manage pertinent and contemporary issues responsibly.

ESSENCE STATEMENT

Woodwork is subject offered at the senior school level, specifically within the Technical Studies track of the STEM pathway. It

builds upon the competencies acquired during Pre-Technical Studies in junior school. The subject equips learners with the

foundational knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values necessary to specialise in Technical Studies at the senior school level.

The subject focuses on the processing of timber and related products to create useful items for society, allowing learners to explore

the unique relationship between trees, wood products, and humanity. It emphasises the sustainable use and management of wood

as a vital natural resource, essential for addressing the challenges of the 21st century. Wood serves as a fundamental material in

woodwork, valued for its beauty, durability, workability, and sustainability, making it ideal for creating both functional and artistic

objects in construction and various crafts. The subject maintains a balance between theoretical and practical work, engaging

learners in projects that connect the content to their local environment. It fosters exploration, imagination, creativity, and

innovation through hands-on projects and practical activities. Learners also gain practical experience by participating in industrial

attachment programs facilitated through partnerships between schools and industry.

The curriculum is structured into four strands: Foundations of Woodwork, Materials, Timber Processes and Products, and Related

Drawing, spanning Grades 10 to 12. Through this structure, learners acquire the knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values necessary

for further training in tertiary institutions or for direct entry into the workforce through apprenticeships. They are prepared to

pursue careers in fields such as wood science, carpentry and joinery, building construction, manufacturing, among others.

viii

SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of senior school, the learner should be able to:

1. Acquire knowledge on career opportunities, employability, and entrepreneurial skills in Woodwork

2. Practice proper health and safety measures in the woodworking workplace

3. Demonstrate skills in identifying, selecting, using, and maintaining woodworking tools, machines, and equipment in the

workplace.

4. Apply acquired skills in the production, processing, storage, selection, and utilisation of timber and other materials for

effective use in woodworking.

5. Use technical drawing skills as a communication tool for planning and designing woodworking products

6. Demonstrate creativity, innovation, and skill in finishing wood products.

7. Appreciate the benefits of evolution of technology and its application in Woodwork
